summary: Preinstall dropper fetches Bun runtime to execute heavily obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's package.json declares a preinstall script `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases at install time and then execFileSync's the Bun binary against a bundled 727KB JavaScript file (math_init.js). math_init.js is heavily obfuscated — rotating string/number array (`n7gIxM=[...]`), hex-mangled identifier names, and index-into-array string accessors — with no source map and no matching source tree in the package. The advertised purpose is a permissions SDK, which has no legitimate need for the Bun runtime or for a native/opaque install-time payload. Fetching an alternate runtime specifically to execute an opaque bundled blob at preinstall is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: the payload runs outside Node's normal boundaries before any import or test surface, and the installer cannot audit what code is executed on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
